definition: Stimulus filtering is the mental process of selecting information that is relevant to the task and reducing the influence of distracting, irrelevant input. In visual working memory, it refers to separating targets from distractors so that behaviorally important items are preferentially represented.

reasons: The packet does not support the general definition-level claim that “stimulus filtering is the mental process of selecting information that is relevant to the task and reducing the influence of distracting, irrelevant input.” It only describes differential brain responses to targets vs. distractors and concludes that dorsal occipital activity “appears to reflect output of stimulus filtering and selection based on behavioral relevance,” without stating the broader “reducing influence” formulation.

The packet supports a relationship between stimulus filtering/selection and separating task-relevant targets from distractors, but it does not explicitly state that, “in visual working memory…behaviorally important items are preferentially represented.” It reports weaker dorsal occipital responses for arrays containing distractors vs. only targets, not preferential representation as a general characterization.
